answers.core: GDScript doesn't offer a way of extending built-in classes, so rather than `vec.clamp_length(2.0)` one would have to do something like `Vector2Util.clamp_length(vec, 2.0)` which is both overly verbose (having to state the explicit type in the function call) and prone to conflict/collisions (this pollutes the global symbol space).
answers.workaround: Yes, it realistically could be handled with only four static methods with 1-line bodies, but I see that as unnecessary boilerplate for such a common, low-level operation. If we have options for `Vector{2,3,4}.normalized()` over `Vector{2,3,4} / Vector{2,3,4}.length()` and `clamp(a, b, c)` over `min(max(a, c), b)` to provide clarity (and performance), I see this no differently.

title: Improve documentation to make `Vector{2,3,4}.limit_length()` easier to find
